To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) The use of macro-glass fibers in the concrete mix reduces the risk of shrinkage cracking in slabs-on-ground.
1) The shrinkage cracking of concrete slabs on a rigid support is mainly governed by the slab thickness and the subgrade modulus.

(1) the addition of glass macro-fibres to concrete is an effective strategy to reduce shrinkage-induced cracks in slabs-on-ground and (2) the use of glass macro-fibre reinforcement can be considered as a viable alternative to conventional reinforcement for the design of slabs-on-ground, in particular in the case of jointless pavement.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues:     1. the effect of different fiber contents (0%, 0.75%, 1.50%, and 2.25% by weight of cement) on the cracking potential in slabs-on-grades due to shrinkage;     2. the effect of the subgrade stiffness on shrinkage cracking;     3. the comparison between the cracking performance of FRC slabs with and without joints.

the following issues: - the influence of slab dimensions, fiber type, and subgrade stiffness on the risk of shrinkage cracking; - the influence of the fiber type, and of the subgrade stiffness on cracking patterns; - the influence on shrinkage cracking due to the presence of a subgrade with different stiffnesses.
the evaluation of the risk of cracking in slabs-on-Grade due to restrained shrinkage.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of glass macro-fibres in slabs-on-ground can be a valid and cost-effective solution to reduce shrinkage cracking.
, in order to obtain an effective control of the cracking due to drying shrinkage, it is necessary to use a high amount of macro-fibers, especially in the case of slabs with a large size.
glass fibers can be considered as a very effective alternative reinforcement to steel mesh and rebars for the control of shrinkage cracking in ground-supported slaps.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of fibers is an effective solution to control shrinkage cracking of slabs-on-grade and that the use of fiber reinforcement is a convenient alternative to conventional reinforcement.
the use of fibers as alternative reinforcement to welded wire mesh is particularly effective to control cracking due to shrinkages.
, for the same level of shrinkage cracking in the slabs-on-grade, the use of fibers allows a reduction of the steel reinforcement.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of fibers is a viable alternative to steel welded mesh and rebars for the design of ground-supported slabs, since the beneficial effects of fibers are particularly convenient in structures subjected to restrained shrinkages.
the beneficial effects of fibers in controlling shrinkage-induced cracking are not only size-dependent but also subgrade-dependent.
, in slabs-on grade, the use of fibers can significantly reduce the risk of cracking.
